subject: Interactions Among Date, Size, and Individual

messages.author: e9bbf555ebd5899d
messages.subject: Interactions Among Date, Size, and Individual
parts:
Hello all!

I have looked through previous threads regarding this issue, but am still struggling to interpret my results here and would greatly appreciate some feedback. The questions I am seeking to answer are: 
    1. Does size have an effect on shape?
     2. If so, does size have a predictable effect on shape?
     3. If so, accounting for size, is shape consistent over time for individuals?

For the purposes of this analysis, I have four sampling dates that I am viewing as discrete groups. I am additionally incorporating log(CSize) and individual ID.

I first determined that there is an effect of size on shape here:
fit.size <- procD.lm(coords ~ log(Csize), data=morph.gdf, iter=999, RRPP= TRUE,
                print.progress = FALSE)
anova(fit.size)

Then, I combined this with date and ID:
commonAllo<procD.lm(coords~log(Csize)+Date*ID,data=morph.gdf,iter=9999,RRPP=T,print.progress=F)
uniqueAllo<procD.lm(coords~log(Csize)*Date*ID,data=morph.gdf,iter=9999,RRPP=T,print.progress=F)

anova(commonAllo,uniqueAllo)

From the output of the uniqueAllo ANOVA (see attached), it appears that Date, cSize, and Date:csize have a significant effect on shape, but ID and the interactions with Date and CSize do not. From my (weak) understanding, this means that shape is not predicted by individual ID, but rather by date and size. 

Am I correct in stating then that individuals of a certain size at a given date will have a given shape? How might I determine if this is true?

I used the plot functions here (https://search.r-project.org/CRAN/refmans/geomorph/html/plotAllometry.html) with method PredLine and regscore to examine this, and while there is overlap between the groups, it appears that the earlier groups (Aug19 and Jan 20) are more similar to each other than the later groups (Sep20 and Jan21). 

So, in an attempt to answer my earlier questions:
     1. Does size have an effect on shape? YES
     2. If so, does size have a predictable effect on shape? MAYBE???
     3. If so, accounting for size, is shape consistent over time for individuals? NO, individual has no effect on shape.

Does anyone have any suggestions for determining one way or another if size has a predictable effect on shape and/or any observations of flaws in this analysis? Additionally, is the best way to present these findings just in the ANOVA output, or is there a more concrete/final way to make a final conclusion with these data?

Thank you for any feedback!! I am so appreciative that this group exists; I have been able to get so much help just by reading threads!

Taylor

If size and date both are affecting shape, what would be the best way to determine if fish of different sizes on the same dates have different shapes? Would stratifying fish by size class or something make sense? Sorry if this is a silly question. I am just trying to explore any possibility with these data. 

Thanks!

messages.author: fbfd20ce829c6c6c
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] Re: Interactions Among Date, Size, and Individual
parts:
Hi Taylor, 

Here are my answers based on your table:

1) size does have an overall effect on shape, but it also depends on date. 

2) The answer to your question depends on what you mean by predictability and what you are looking to predict. E.g., the effect is significant therefore size changes shape in a predictable manner equal to the beta coefficients in your model. Or maybe you are referring to prediction of individual sample values.

3) Is shape consistent over time? No, date has a significant effect. After accounting for size? Your interaction implies the effect of date on shape depends on size. You can try something like pairwise(uniqueAllo, groups = morph.gdf$Date). Please see the pairwise.lm.rrpp help page for details.

However, I get the impression you might also be asking whether individuals, and not the mean shape of all individuals changes between dates. If so, you might run a regression model where Y = Individual1.Time1 - Individual1.Time2 and so on for all individuals, and regress onto size. This will tell you if individual shape differences between time points, rather than mean shape for the whole group, depends on size.
"what would be the best way to determine if fish of different sizes on the same dates have different shapes? "

Your model here sounds like you are interested in subsetting your data to keep only data from one date. From there you can regress shape onto size and I believe that gets at your question.

Best,
Bryan
